bull.b: Securing long-term power directly addresses a core requirement for the Texas data-center project and reduces exposure to future procurement uncertainty. The contracted Phase 1 supply can support tenant discussions, improve project bankability, and provide a durable foundation for development through 2027.

The combination of substantial land control, expanded planned capacity, and a larger master plan creates room for multi-phase growth beyond the initial facility. If execution milestones are achieved, this pipeline could support recurring infrastructure revenues and improve operating scale over time.

Recent capital actions provide resources to repay debt, fund working capital, and advance project development while leasing discussions continue. Access to staged project financing and substantial reported liquidity improves near-term execution capacity, although future draws remain tied to specified milestones.

bear.b: The existing business is not yet generating sufficient revenue or profit to fund operations, with losses worsening as revenue remains small. Persistent operating and free-cash-flow deficits increase reliance on external capital and make successful project execution important to any future improvement in earnings quality.

The equity raise strengthens available funding but materially expands the share count, diluting existing holders and demonstrating the capital intensity of the strategy. Continued reliance on equity, debt, and project-level financing could constrain financial flexibility if construction or leasing needs exceed current resources.

The project’s targeted 2027 readiness depends on several linked commercial, financing, permitting, and site-readiness steps rather than on completed construction alone. Delays in any major condition could postpone revenue generation, weaken tenant conversion, and extend the period of corporate cash burn.
